Sam L: Hey team — noticed a regression on TP4 int8 runs after yesterday's kernel selector change. P50 latency +28% and throughput down ~15% compared to last good. Repro on 4xA100. Any quick ideas?
perf-ci-bot: queued perf job 82734 — results link: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/82734 :eyes:
Maria G: I ran a 100-step profile on the same rig. Main issue looks like all-reduce sitting on the critical path instead of overlapping with compute. Snippet from nsys:```
Time (ms) | Operation
--------------------------------
2.22      | GEMM compute (stage 1)
1.82      | Allreduce (NVLink)
2.05      | GEMM compute (stage 2)
1.60      | GPU idle / waiting for comm
```
Maria G: Also saw KV cache churn at stage boundaries; hit_rate ~0.17 in the first 200 tokens which forces repeated KV serialization/deserialization.
Jake P: What batch size / tokens-per-request? Could be batching heuristic + TP boundary causing small microbatches and extra allreduces.
Sam L: Default request shape: batch=8, tokens=512, dynamic batching ENABLED (auto).
Jake P: Try forcing larger batching window or pinch token batcher: `--batcher-max-delay=25 --batcher-max-size=12` might reduce allreduce calls. Also check kernel selection: int8 path is falling back to a slower GEMM for matmul with sequence lengths >384.
Maria G: Confirmed — kernel selector log shows fallback on the attention matmul: `selected_kernel: matmul_generic_int8` instead of `matmul_fused_int8`. That fallback coincides with the TP boundary in our shim, which increases comm frequency.
Sam L: Any experiments with fp8? Was FP8 immune?
Maria G: FP8 measured higher raw throughput but we triggered occasional numeric saturation on longer prompts (scaling factor stability). FP8 had better overlap because its fused kernels keep compute longer and allow all-reduce batching, but numerical drift made us hesitant to flip in prod.
Anu S: Two quick knobs: 1) enable async all-reduce (NCCL_ASYNC_PTHREADS=1) to unblock GPU compute while communication proceeds; 2) prefer fused kernels across TP boundaries — add a kernel-hint for the attention path. Also try `NCCL_ALGO=Tree` or tune `NCCL_MAX_NTHREADS`.
Jake P: Proposed tiny change to kernel selector (pseudo):```c++
if (is_int8 && tp_degree > 1 && seq_len <= 1024) {
  prefer_kernel("matmul_fused_int8_attention");
}
```
Jake P: That avoids the generic path that increases CPU-side work and stalls.
Maria G: Repro command I'm going to run on the lab cluster:```bash
RUNTIME_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_PROFILE=nsys \
NCCL_ASYNC_PTHREADS=1 NCCL_ALGO=Tree \
./redwood-run --model gptx-medium --tp 4 --dtype int8 \
--batch 8 --tokens 512 --batcher-max-delay 25 --kv-cache on \
--seed 42 --steps 100
```
Maria G: Expected after change: allreduce per-step < 1.0ms (from 1.8ms), GPU idle time near 0.3ms, overall p50 down to baseline.
Sam L: I'll provision the 4xA100 slot and run Maria's command. I'll also try with `--dtype fp8` on a separate run to reproduce numeric issues.
perf-ci-bot: job 82734 started on lab-a100-04; logs: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/82734/logs
Anu S: If you see KV cache hit rate still low, look at our per-shard key layout — we may be reshuffling keys at TP boundaries. A quick mitigation is sticky KV placement: `--kv-shard-affinity=stage-local` which reduces cross-stage KV transfer.
Sam L: Thanks — will report back with numbers. If this fixes perf we can land the kernel-hint and add a CI perf test that asserts allreduce <= 1.2ms on TP4 int8. :thumbsup:
